name: Tà Chì Nhù
headline: Above the clouds, beneath the night sky.

images.title: Moonburst Above the Cloud Sea
images.story: We stepped out into the biting wind to find the entire valley smothered under a thick blanket of white clouds. The moon was burning bright enough to cast a sharp starburst through the lens, but the higher sky remained packed with cold, pinprick stars. Up here, it felt less like standing on a mountain and more like looking out of an airplane window at midnight.

images.title: Sunburst Along the Ridge
images.story: Heavy storm clouds had spent most of the late afternoon rolling over the crest, threatening to wipe out the sunset entirely. Then, for about two minutes, the sun found a narrow seam right along the ridgeline and flared in a harsh amber burst. It was not the clean golden hour we had planned for, but the contrast was much better.

images.title: Pastel Glow Behind the Peaks
images.story: As the sun sank behind the jagged peaks, the harsh glare softened into a muted peach band across the horizon. Cold fog started tumbling up the slope from the left, curling over the dark saddle of the ridge. You could already feel the temperature plummeting the second that warm light faded.

images.title: Field of Pinpoint Stars
images.story: Once the wind chased off the last low clouds, the sky overhead turned completely ink-black. There was zero light pollution up here, just thousands of faint pinpoint stars and the hazy dusting of the Milky Way. Tilting the camera straight up felt like aiming a lens into deep space.

images.title: Tarp Shelter Under the Stars
images.story: The rustic mountain shack was not winning any architectural awards with its blue tarp and firewood counterweights, but it kept the wind off our backs. Stepping just outside the doorway framed the Milky Way right above the tin roofline. It is hard to complain about rough sleeping conditions when your front porch looks like this.

images.title: Milky Way Over the Ridge
images.story: By late evening, the core of the galaxy tilted diagonally across the northern ridgeline. The dark contour of the mountain gave the massive starfield a sense of scale you rarely get from an open sky shot. My fingers were nearly numb on the tripod dial, but the framing was worth standing out in the cold.

images.title: Galactic Core Over the Saddle
images.story: Stepping out of the wooden shelter into freezing air, the sky was completely open with no city glow for miles. The galactic core stretched diagonally across the dark, resting just above the silhouette of the ridge. Standing on the frozen turf, all you could hear was the wind cutting through the saddle.

images.title: Headlamp Starburst at First Light
images.story: We started the summit push well before dawn, chasing the thin orange strip burning along the horizon. On the higher ridge ahead, another group paused, their headlamp throwing a bright starburst against the twilight. Below us, the cloud inversion sat perfectly still like an endless white floor.

images.title: Summit Push in the Dark
images.story: A few hundred meters below the peak, the horizon began to split into burnt orange and cold dawn blue. Someone clicked on a headlamp to check the footing, painting a patch of green grass against the black hill. It was too steep to talk, so we just kept matching each other's pace.

images.title: Cloud Ocean at Dawn
images.story: By six in the morning, the valley was entirely buried under a dense white floor of clouds that stretched to the distant ranges. The jagged crests looked like islands poking through water, backlit by the soft amber band on the horizon. The wind finally died down, leaving just the cold ridge and quiet view.

images.title: Mountain Bouquet and Beanie
images.story: Once the sun climbed higher, the chill gave way to blinding light and some trail humor. She gathered a scrappy bouquet of dried mountain shrubs, striking an impromptu runway pose with her sunglasses and pink beanie. The trekking pole made the whole high-altitude fashion statement surprisingly convincing.

images.title: Blue Scarf in Morning Sun
images.story: To shield against the mountain breeze, she wrapped a vibrant blue scarf around her head, holding on to the dried wildflower bundle we picked earlier. The low morning light caught the side of the ridge, with valleys of soft cloud drifting far below. Her expression turned unexpectedly solemn for just a split second before laughing again.

images.title: Warm Smiles Under the Tarp
images.story: Taking a breather under a makeshift tarp shelter, I crossed paths with a girl holding her cheerful younger sibling. Wrapped in an oversized pink windbreaker and completely unbothered by bare feet in the mountain air, the toddler gave my lens an infectious grin. It was an easy, genuine moment that made me instantly forget about tired legs.
